title: Reading: True/False/Not Given
focus: Distinguir contradição, confirmação e ausência de dados
verifiableTask: Justificar oito classificações com trechos do texto

content.text: nada sobre isso (nem sim, nem não).
Ao final da aula você consegue:
justificar oito classificações com trechos do texto.
O professor diz um fato sobre o aluno; outra pessoa “afirma” algo. True, False ou Not Given?
Ana lives in Recife and works as a nurse.
1. Ana lives in Brazil. (T) · 2. Ana is a doctor. (F) · 3. Ana likes her job. (NG) · 4. Ana works in a hospital. (?)
qual é a diferença entre skim e scan?
Palavras que mudam tudo (leia com lupa!)
more than / less than / the first / the only / the largest
before / after / since / until / originally / now
The text says… which means… so it's True.
The text mentions X, but it doesn't say anything about Y, so it's Not Given.
The text mentions the price, but it doesn't say anything about the quality, so it's Not Given.

questions.questionText: The text says the opposite of the statement. The answer is…
The text says nothing about the statement. The answer is…
Text: “Researchers suggested that…”. Statement: “Researchers proved that…”. The statement is…

options.text: False or Not Given — the level of certainty is different

explanations.B: Correto: cuidado com o grau de certeza.
explanations.general: Correct answer: False or Not Given — the level of certainty is different

questions.questionText: “Not Given” means the statement is false.

explanations.general: Falso: NG significa que não há informação.

content.text: pela âncora (as afirmações seguem a ordem do texto).
The Great Barrier Reef, located off the coast of Queensland, is the world's largest coral reef system. Since 1995, it has lost more than half of its coral, mainly due to rising sea temperatures.
The reef is near the coast of Queensland.
located off the coast of Queensland
The reef is the largest in the world.
The reef has lost less than half of its coral since 1995.
Tourism is the main cause of coral loss.
mainly due to rising sea temperatures
) — o texto dá outra causa principal.
The reef attracts two million tourists a year.
→ True / “the world's largest” / “the largest in the world” → Not Given / the text mentions temperature / it doesn't mention tourists

Honey never spoils if it is stored correctly. Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were around 3,000 years old and still edible. This is because honey contains very little water and is naturally acidic, which prevents bacteria from growing. However, if honey absorbs moisture from the air, it can ferment.
Honey can last for thousands of years.
All the honey found in Egyptian tombs was edible.
Honey contains a lot of water.
Honey can ferment if it absorbs moisture.

questions.questionText: Honey can last for thousands of years.
All the honey found in Egyptian tombs was edible.

explanations.general: O texto fala de “pots of honey” encontrados comestíveis, mas não diz que TODO o mel era comestível.

questions.questionText: Honey contains a lot of water.
Honey can ferment if it absorbs moisture.

explanations.general: “if honey absorbs moisture from the air, it can ferment”.
O texto não fala de uso medicinal.

questions.questionText: Tourism is the main cause of coral loss in the Great Barrier Reef.

explanations.general: O texto diz que a causa principal é o aumento da temperatura do mar.

content.text: Shared electric scooters first appeared in Santa Monica, California, in 2017, and within two years they were available in more than 100 cities worldwide. Users unlock the scooters with a smartphone app and pay by the minute.

Supporters claim that e-scooters reduce car journeys, but research so far is mixed. A study in Paris found that most scooter trips replaced walking or public transport rather than car trips. In addition, the scooters themselves often last only a few months, which raises questions about their environmental benefits.

Safety is another concern. Hospitals in several cities have reported an increase in head injuries, and some cities, including Madrid, have temporarily banned the scooters. Others have introduced speed limits and designated parking areas.
Despite these problems, operators have improved the design of their vehicles, and newer models are said to last considerably longer.
Shared e-scooters were first introduced in California.
By 2019, e-scooters were available in over 100 cities.
Users pay a fixed price per trip.
The Paris study showed that most scooter trips replaced car trips.
Early scooters had a short lifespan.
Some cities have created special parking areas for scooters.
Newer scooters are cheaper to rent.
Para cada resposta, leia em voz alta o trecho que prova (ou diga “the text doesn't mention…”).
[ ] Usou só o texto (não conhecimento próprio)?
